Verification Codes AutoFill settings vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume iOS security-code AutoFill covers storefront language. System OTP parsing, keyboard suggestions, and App Store Connect actually separate fill behavior from product-page copy:

  • Settings → Passwords → AutoFill Passwords & Passkeys → AutoFill verification codes — toggle on the buyer's iPhone or iPad that lets iOS offer one-time SMS and email security codes above the keyboard. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • From Messages / Mail code suggestions — when an SMS or email contains a numeric verification code, iOS may surface it in the QuickType bar so the buyer taps once to fill the OTP field. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains one-tap code entry to China storefront readers.
  • Verification field detection — apps mark OTP inputs with one-time-code content types so the system knows where to insert parsed codes. Your listing may show a code-fill demo; wiring text fields is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • SMS domain association — optional developer setup so Messages trusts OTP senders for AutoFill. Listing copy may mention reliable code delivery; configuring associated domains is engineering — AppLocale does not touch it.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of AutoFill verification codes capability on device.

Working OTP AutoFill UX in the app and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.
